A guide for you — with real screenshots

One agent that actually knows your work — so people stop asking you for status updates.

Agent Org Mesh gives everyone in your organization a personal agent that stays current on their real work. When someone needs an update, they ask your agent instead of interrupting you — and it answers using only what's true, and only what you and your organization have agreed is okay to share. Every screenshot below is the real product, not a mockup.

Getting set up

Meet Diego Okonjo, a Staff Engineer on the Payments team at Northbeam. Four steps, done once — this is exactly what he saw.

1

Find yourself in your organization

Your organization is already set up with everyone's name and reporting line. Just find yourself in the switcher — nothing to fill in.

2

Land on your agent

This is home. You immediately see what your agent is connected to and how much of your work it can currently see — nothing is hidden from you, ever, starting with this very first screen.

3

Choose your main agent

Pick which assistant represents you, and decide how much it's allowed to see: the full picture, or a narrower slice you set yourself. You can change this any time.

4

Connect your real tools

Connect the tools you actually use. For most, it's one paste: generate a read-only key from the tool itself, paste it in, done. For tools that run on your own machine, your agent hands you a key instead — and that tool reports its own real activity straight back.

Real activity only — never invented

What Diego sees back

Diego didn't have to ask anyone what Hana wanted to know. It's already sitting in his own agent, waiting for him — switch identity back to Diego and this is what's there.

Ask yourself, anytime

You don't need someone else to ask about you to get value from your agent. On your own home screen, there's a real, ongoing conversation with it — the same honest answers, the same real evidence, just for your own use.

Pick up where you left off

Every conversation is saved for real — close the tab, come back tomorrow, and it's exactly as you left it.

Start fresh whenever you want

One click starts a brand-new conversation with no memory of the last one — useful when you're switching topics entirely.

Still the same honest rules

Asking yourself still goes through the same real check as anyone else asking about you — it's simply a question only you could truthfully ask.

What you can always count on

These aren't settings someone could quietly turn off. They're built into how the system works.

Read-only, always

Nothing here ever changes your actual tools or accounts. It only reads — it never posts, edits, or deletes anything on your behalf.

Nothing is invented

Every answer is built only from your real, connected activity. If there's nothing real to say, it says that — never a guess dressed up as fact.

Some things are simply never touched

Pay, performance reviews, legal matters, health information, private messages — no agent can ever see these. It's not a setting anyone can enable.

You always know who asked

Every real question about you is recorded permanently in your own history — who asked, what they claimed their relationship to you was, and exactly what they got back.

Nothing is silently hidden

If something can't be shared, both you and the person asking see exactly that — never a blank space that looks like nothing happened.

You can fix mistakes

If your agent gets something wrong, correct it in one place and explain what's actually true — it disappears from every future answer immediately.

You control what's connected

Connect or disconnect any tool, any time. A narrower connection simply means less is shared — and it's always visible on your own coverage page.

Take your data with you

Download everything held about you — every claim, its source, and every time someone asked — as a real file, any time you want it.

The record can't be rewritten

Once a question is answered, that record is permanent. A later change to the sharing rules can never quietly change what someone was already told.

What gets flagged automatically

You shouldn't have to notice everything yourself. The system watches for a few specific, real situations and quietly raises them to the right person — nothing sits unnoticed.

Someone's not connected

A person who's supposed to be covered has nothing real feeding their agent.

→

Or things went quiet

A connected tool stopped reporting anything new for a while.

→

Automatically flagged

No one has to spot it — the system raises it on its own.

→

Shown to the right person

Whoever's actually in a position to help — your manager, or IT — sees it and can act.

Also flagged: when the same person keeps genuinely being blocked from information they should reasonably be able to get — a sign the sharing rules might need a second look, not something to leave unnoticed.

If you're setting up the organization

A quick note for whoever sets this up for the first time — everyone else can skip this.

1

Build the chart

Create your organization, then add people one by one — name, title, team, and who they report to.

2

Set the sharing rules

Decide, per relationship (manager, peer, executive, IT...), how much of each kind of information they can get — shared in full, a limited hint, or not shared. Change it any time; it never rewrites what's already been told to someone.

3

Watch it work

See coverage across the whole organization, every real question that's been asked, and anything that's been automatically flagged for attention.
